label: The commutator where a ring settles
title: A commutator that varies globally can be constant on a finite ring's eventual image
kind: Exact algebra and exhaustive finite-ring computation
summary: On periodic rings of 8 to 20 cells, 47 elementary rules beyond the affine rules and Rules 4 and 200 have a constant commutator on the states that lie on cycles. The constant is all-zeros or all-ones because the commutator respects the ring shift. A conjectured ceiling at period two is refuted by Rules 44 and 100, which carry a period-three wave exactly when the width is a multiple of three.
takeaway: Most attractor-constancy is a fixed-point triviality, the two-valued outcome is forced by symmetry, and a claim required to hold at every ring size can hide a commensurability counterexample.
